anatomy.title: Anatomy of a Prosecution
anatomy.subtitle: The very same transaction has been upheld by courts as lawful — and charged as a crime.
anatomy.text: We are not asking for an acquittal. We are asking for one thing: that every piece of available evidence be examined. This site layers the case from the ground up — commercial contracts, criminal proceedings, international mechanisms. The documents speak. Readers can judge for themselves.
anatomy.manifesto: The moment we treat this extradition request as legitimate, we prise open a Pandora's box in international law. Extradition stops being an instrument of justice and becomes a mechanism for state-sanctioned abduction. Any government in the world will be able to eliminate opponents across borders by writing the right criminal-code article on a request form. Serbia's compliance turns international legal cooperation into a tool for extrajudicial retribution — where a formal piece of paper outweighs a human life and the binding court rulings of the very state making the request. This is not justice. It is complicity in transnational repression.

legal.title: ⚖️ Legal Dissonance
legal.text: Russian arbitration courts — right up to the Supreme Court — found the transaction lawful. The criminal prosecution treats the same transaction as fraud. The investigators' own records quote Lagovsky writing 'the value must be real' — and cite this as proof of a conspiracy to understate value. A state that inverts the meaning of its own documents does not merely harm one person: it erodes the very foundation of the rule of law.
legal.question: Can insisting on a fair market value be evidence of a conspiracy to suppress it?

international.title: 🌍 International Dimension
international.text: This case has moved well beyond a bilateral dispute. Serbia, Interpol, the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention, the ECHR — each of these institutions exists precisely to check whether the rule of law is being upheld where domestic mechanisms have failed. This is not pressure on a court. This is exactly what international law was built for.

sidebar.title: Press Coverage
sidebar.manifesto: The press archive is not a news feed — it is an independent audit of the case. Every publication collected here reflects facts that professional journalists have put on record: the contradictions in the Lagovsky case are real and documented.

news.title: Serbian court refused to hear defence evidence — only formal paperwork from Moscow counted
news.desc: The Court of Appeal was unambiguous: it was interested only in the document it had received, not in the substance of the allegations. The underlying transaction has been found lawful by arbitration courts through to the Russian Supreme Court — none of those rulings were considered.
news.focus: Defence counsel documented concrete violations: insufficient grounds for reasonable suspicion — the baseline requirement for extradition — plus the fact that the requesting state has withdrawn from both the UN Convention Against Torture and the Council of Europe. N1 is a CNN-affiliated broadcaster; the report puts these violations on the record through an independent outlet.

news.title: Serbia one step from extradition: decision now rests with the Minister of Justice
news.desc: On 3 December the Belgrade Court of Appeal confirmed that the conditions for extradition are met. The final decision has been referred to the Minister of Justice — the last stage in this procedure, with no further avenue for appeal.
news.focus: Defence lawyer Marko Štambuk notes that in practice Serbian ministers of justice very rarely refuse extradition once the courts have established formal grounds. Coverage in a pan-European media network signals that the case has moved beyond the Serbian legal sphere.

news.title: Interpol CCF confirms: complaint accepted, Red Notice under review
news.desc: The Interpol Commission for the Control of Files (CCF) notified the defence that its challenge to the Red Notice has been accepted for review (ref. CCF/135/R1610.25). Russia issued the notice on 25 January 2025, based on an in-absentia arrest warrant issued on 27 December 2024.
news.focus: The defence is invoking Article 3 of the Interpol Constitution, which bars the organisation from involvement in matters of a commercial nature. The transaction at the heart of the charges has been found lawful by courts up to the Russian Supreme Court — this is the core argument. A secondary argument: the Red Notice itself describes Lagovsky as an 'enterprise engineer', directly contradicting his actual status as a self-employed independent lawyer, documented by service contracts, acceptance certificates and payment records.
